name: archive.today (retrieval)
notes: Independent snapshot service that disregards robots exclusions and captures pages the Wayback Machine will not, including many social-media pages. Rotates between mirror domains - a request to archive.today was observed landing on archive.ph, and archive.is and archive.li serve the same corpus - and it suffers periodic DNS and availability problems. The operator is anonymous - fine as a lead, weaker as evidence provenance than Internet Archive.

name: archive.today (submission)
notes: Submitting a URL triggers a live fetch of the target and produces a permanently public snapshot at a shareable short URL. Same exposure trade-off as Save Page Now, with the added issue that you cannot later withdraw the capture.

name: Arquivo.pt
jurisdiction_notes: Portuguese national web archive; deepest coverage of .pt and Portuguese-language sites, including Lusophone Africa and Brazil to a lesser degree.
notes: Its distinguishing feature is full-text search across archived page content, which the Wayback Machine does not offer for the general web - you can find an archived page by a phrase inside it instead of needing to already know the URL. Has a documented public API.

name: Common Crawl
notes: Free multi-petabyte web crawl published as monthly archives with a per-crawl URL index. The way to enumerate every URL and hostname seen under a domain across years without sending it a single request. Requires bulk-data handling, and per-site coverage is a sample rather than an exhaustive crawl.

name: Ghostarchive
notes: Archives material other services handle badly, notably YouTube videos and social-media posts, and preserves the media itself rather than an empty page shell. This row covers retrieval of existing captures only; submitting a URL for archiving triggers a live fetch of the target and is active, on the same terms as Save Page Now. Community-run with no institutional backing or funding guarantee - mirror anything you intend to rely on into your own evidence directory immediately.

name: Wayback Machine (retrieval)
notes: Reading existing captures is entirely passive - the target never learns of it. The general-purpose source for deleted pages, superseded staff listings, former contact details and changed terms. Robots-based exclusions and takedown requests silently remove some captures, so a gap is not proof a page never existed. Google cache: was retired in 2024, making this the default fallback for a dead URL.

name: Wayback Machine Save Page Now
notes: The save form was confirmed present and reachable without an account; an archive.org login raises the limits and unlocks options such as capturing outlinks. Saving makes Internet Archive fetch the URL from its own infrastructure, so the target logs show an archive.org crawler hit at the moment you looked, and the resulting capture is public immediately. Excellent for evidence integrity, poor for a quiet investigation. Snapshot at the end of collection, or accept the exposure as a deliberate decision recorded in the ledger.

name: Have I Been Pwned
jurisdiction_notes: Notification service only: it tells you WHETHER an address appeared in a known breach and names the breach. It never serves passwords or record contents, which is exactly what makes it usable where handling a breach corpus would not be. Domain-wide search requires proving control of the domain, so it is a self-audit tool and not a way to enumerate someone else's staff.
notes: The reference source for breach exposure. Each breach entry carries a date, a record count and the data classes exposed, which is enough to reason about what a target may have had stolen without ever touching the corpus. The free web lookup now sits behind a Cloudflare Turnstile challenge, so it is a manual browser step and cannot be scripted — do not attempt to defeat the challenge; use the paid API key instead if you need automation. Absence is weak evidence — unindexed and unreported breaches exist.

name: Mozilla Monitor
jurisdiction_notes: Same notification-only posture as HIBP. Consumer-facing and designed for checking your own address.
notes: Renamed from Firefox Monitor. Breach data has historically been licensed from Have I Been Pwned, so treat a hit here as the same source restated rather than independent corroboration of a HIBP hit unless you can confirm the current data source. The added value is the paid data-broker removal service, which is genuinely useful in a self-audit engagement. The free one-off scan needs no account; continuous alerting needs a Mozilla account.

name: Pwned Passwords
jurisdiction_notes: Built around k-anonymity: you submit only the first five characters of a SHA-1 hash and match the remainder locally, so the service never learns which password you checked. That design is what makes it acceptable against credentials you legitimately hold.
notes: Tells you whether a password hash appears in aggregated breach corpora and how often. Legitimate uses: self-audit, and checking a credential you already lawfully possess during an authorised engagement. It is a hash oracle, not a people lookup — it cannot map a password back to a person. The full hash-prefix dataset is downloadable for offline use.

name: deps.dev
notes: Google Open Source Insights: cross-ecosystem dependency graphs, licences, advisories and source repository links for packages on npm, PyPI, Maven, Go, Cargo, NuGet and others. In an investigation it maps an organisation's published packages to the repositories and maintainer accounts behind them, and shows what a target's software actually depends on. For typosquat and supply-chain questions compare a suspect package's declared repository against the real one - a mismatch is the tell. The registries themselves also expose maintainer accounts that pivot to usernames and, on older packages, to email addresses.

name: GH Archive
rate_limit: Hourly archive files are freely downloadable; BigQuery access is billed by Google.
notes: Hourly archive of the public GitHub event stream going back to 2011, queryable in bulk. This is how you recover what was deleted: repositories that were removed, commits that were force-pushed away, issue and comment text that was edited, and the timeline of a username before it was renamed. Push event payloads have historically carried commit author names and email addresses. Volume is large enough that ad-hoc grep is impractical - plan for a query engine.

name: GitHub Code Search
rate_limit: Code search requires a signed-in account; limits unknown.
jurisdiction_notes: Content may be removed under DMCA or by the owner; capture and hash anything you rely on at the time you find it.
notes: Search across public code, commits, issues and users. High-value queries are an organisation email domain in commit metadata, internal hostnames, S3 and storage bucket names, and configuration filenames. Commit history is the richest part: author name and email are attached to every commit and frequently include personal addresses that never appear on the profile, and force-pushed or deleted content often survives in forks, pull requests and the events archive. Searching does not notify the repository owner; starring, forking, following or opening an issue does.

name: grep.app
notes: Regex search across a large crawl of public GitHub repositories without needing an account, and faster than GitHub's own search for a literal string across many repos. Index is a third-party crawl, so it is a subset and can lag - a negative result here does not mean the string is not on GitHub. Good for finding a leaked internal hostname, key prefix or unusual identifier across unrelated projects. A Vercel security checkpoint rate-limits and blocks scripted fetches, so the endpoint is recorded verified=no; it loads in a browser. That checkpoint also rules out driving it from a script.

name: Software Heritage
jurisdiction_notes: Operates a takedown policy; archived content can be removed on request.
notes: Long-term archive of publicly available source code harvested from GitHub, GitLab, PyPI, Debian and other origins, preserving full development history with content-addressed identifiers. The correct place to look when a repository has been deleted from its origin - the archived copy retains commits, authorship and timestamps. Harvesting is periodic rather than continuous, so very recent work may not be present, and coverage of a specific repository is not guaranteed. The homepage recorded here is confirmed; the archive host at archive.softwareheritage.org serves a proof-of-work bot interstitial to scripted requests and loads only in a browser, so do not plan on fetching it from a script.

name: TruffleHog
jurisdiction_notes: Verifying a discovered credential means authenticating to a live service with someone else's secret. Without explicit written authorisation that is likely unauthorised access under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, the UK Computer Misuse Act and equivalents. Do not run verification outside an engagement scope that names it.
notes: Scans repositories, filesystems and archives for credentials, including the full git history where secrets are most often found after being removed from the current tree. Marked active because the default behaviour verifies discovered credentials against the issuing service, which is an authenticated request to a third party - disable verification to keep the scan passive. Cloning a public repository from a code host is passive; scanning a self-hosted git server belonging to the target is not. Gitleaks is a comparable scanner with a different rule set - run both when the question is whether anything leaked.

name: ABN Lookup
jurisdiction_notes: Australia. Free public search of the Australian Business Register returning ABN, entity name, entity type, GST registration status, effective dates, and the state and postcode of the main business location. The full street address is not published.
notes: Fast confirmation that a trading name maps to a real registered entity and whether it is GST-registered, which is a cheap liveness test on an Australian counterparty. Trading and business name history is included and is useful for tracing rebrands. Web search needs no login or key, so auth is none; the separate machine interface requires a free registered GUID.

name: ACRA BizFile+
jurisdiction_notes: Singapore. Free search returns entity name, Unique Entity Number, status and incorporation date. The Business Profile containing directors, shareholders with shareholdings and the registered address is a paid purchase per entity. Singapore's register of registrable controllers is filed with ACRA but is not public.
notes: The paid Business Profile is inexpensive and lists shareholders with exact holdings - unusually good ownership data for the price. A large nominee-director industry operates in Singapore, so a director appearing on dozens of unrelated entities is a corporate services provider, not a principal; treat that as a signal to find the provider's client, not as a finding. ACRA entity data is also republished as an open dataset on the government data portal.

name: ADGM Public Register
jurisdiction_notes: Abu Dhabi Global Market only - a separate common-law jurisdiction inside the UAE. Entities registered in mainland Abu Dhabi or in other emirates and free zones are not here. Mainland UAE Department of Economic Development registers are not publicly searchable and the UAE has no consolidated national company search.
notes: Registered entities with status, licence category, registered address and in many cases directors. ADGM and DIFC are the only two UAE registers a researcher can meaningfully query; for everything else the realistic routes are a trade licence copy obtained from the counterparty, a local agent, litigation records, or a commercial data provider. The site reorganises periodically, so re-derive the path from the ADGM home page if the recorded one moves.

name: ASIC Connect
jurisdiction_notes: Australia. Free search of company name, ACN, status and registration date; the current and historical company extract containing directors, shareholders and addresses is a paid purchase. ASIC separately publishes banned and disqualified persons and its licensee registers free of charge.
notes: The paid extract is the substantive document - it lists directors, secretaries and the top members with their shareholdings, which makes Australia one of the better-value jurisdictions for real ownership data. Always also check the banned and disqualified persons register and the credit and financial services licensee registers. A registered business name is not a legal person; resolve it to a company or a sole trader before drawing conclusions. Marked unverified because the host root redirects unauthenticated scripted requests into an authentication loop and the search application is JavaScript-only; ASIC's own register index at https://www.asic.gov.au/online-services/search-asic-registers/ was confirmed live and is the reliable way in.

name: BVI Financial Services Commission
jurisdiction_notes: British Virgin Islands. There is no public company register. Company records are held through licensed registered agents via the VIRRGIN system, accessible to agents and authorities only, and the BOSS beneficial ownership system is available solely to designated competent authorities. A public register has been announced and deferred repeatedly - do not assume one exists without checking.
notes: What you can actually obtain from the FSC site is the list of licensed and regulated financial services entities, enforcement notices, public statements, and struck-off or liquidation notices. For an ordinary BVI business company the realistic routes are the BVI Commercial Court record, the ICIJ leak databases, filings by a listed parent that consolidates the entity, or a lawful request through the registered agent. Treat a BVI entity as a name and a formation date until something else corroborates it. The host requires ordinary browser headers.

name: California bizfile Online
jurisdiction_notes: California. Statements of Information filed by corporations and LLCs name officers, directors and the manager or member, and the filed images are free to view. Registered agent may be a commercial agent rather than a principal.
notes: Free entity search plus free PDF images of filed documents including the Statement of Information - unusually generous for a US state. Statements are filed annually for corporations and biennially for LLCs, so officer data can be up to two years stale. Also covers limited partnerships, LLPs and foreign entities qualified to do business in California, which is how out-of-state shells become visible. The site rejects requests that do not present ordinary browser headers.

name: Cayman Islands General Registry
jurisdiction_notes: Cayman Islands. No free public register. The General Registry offers a chargeable name search and certificate ordering; directors, shareholders and beneficial owners are not public. The beneficial ownership regime files data with a competent authority rather than the public, and a public-access commitment has been repeatedly postponed. CIMA separately publishes regulated funds, administrators and licensees.
notes: Expect to confirm existence and status and little else. For substance use the CIMA regulated-entity lists, the Cayman Grand Court cause list and published judgments, filings by an affiliated listed group in the US or UK, and the leak databases. A Cayman entity in a structure is normally the fund or holding layer - the operating business and the identifiable people almost always sit in another jurisdiction, so pivot outward rather than digging here.

name: Charity Commission Register of Charities
jurisdiction_notes: England and Wales only. Scotland (OSCR) and Northern Ireland (CCNI) maintain separate registers with different rules. Trustee names are public; trustee addresses are not.
notes: Trustees, annual accounts and returns, income and expenditure, and any statutory inquiry or regulatory action taken by the Commission. Trustee name search links an individual to other charities, and the trustee overlap graph is worth building because charities are a common route for moving funds and for reputation-building. Accounts filing lags the financial year end by up to ten months, so a recently failed charity may still look healthy.

name: Corporations Canada
jurisdiction_notes: Federal CBCA corporations only, which are a minority of Canadian companies. Each province runs its own register with different fees and openness - Quebec's REQ is free and unusually detailed, British Columbia charges. Canada launched a public register of individuals with significant control over CBCA corporations in January 2024, covering federally incorporated companies only.
notes: Federal corporation search returns directors, registered office and status. The federal individuals-with-significant-control search is a genuine open beneficial ownership source and one of very few in the Americas - but it stops at the federal boundary, so a provincially incorporated company is invisible to it. The department migrated from the ic.gc.ca domain and old bookmarks now redirect; the search path recorded here was confirmed live.

name: CourtListener
jurisdiction_notes: US federal courts plus a large set of state appellate courts. Federal docket coverage comes from the RECAP archive, which contains only documents someone has already purchased and contributed - it is broad but not complete, and absence proves nothing.
notes: Free full-text search across opinions and RECAP dockets, plus oral argument audio and judge profiles, run by the Free Law Project. Always search here before spending money in PACER, because a large share of significant dockets is already mirrored. An API and bulk data are offered. It is a mirror, so aggregation is not corroboration - the citable primary is the court's own opinion or the PACER docket entry, and a document held here should be cited to the issuing court.

name: Delaware Division of Corporations
jurisdiction_notes: Delaware is the highest-volume US incorporation jurisdiction and one of the least disclosive. The free entity search returns name, file number, incorporation date and registered agent only. Officers, directors, members, shareholders and beneficial owners are not published. Filing detail and annual report data must be ordered for a fee.
notes: Confirms existence, status and formation date and gives the registered agent, which is often the only usable pivot. Expect a commercial agent address, never an operating address. For the humans behind a Delaware entity, go to litigation records, SEC filings, state occupational licensing, or the foreign-qualification filing in the state where the company actually trades. Wyoming, Nevada and New Mexico offer comparable or greater opacity.

name: Denmark CVR
jurisdiction_notes: Denmark. Among the most open registers in Europe: free search by company, by person and by address, exposing management, board membership, legal owners and significant ownership, plus filed annual reports. Denmark has continued to publish substantial ownership data, though the real-owner field was affected by the 2022 CJEU ruling - check what the register currently returns rather than assuming.
notes: Person search returns every Danish directorship and ownership stake held by an individual with full history, which is a rare capability among national registers. Annual reports are free PDFs. Bulk and machine access is offered through the Virk platform. Danish holding structures appear frequently in Nordic and shipping ownership chains, so this register often resolves a link that stalls elsewhere. Marked unverified because the host answers scripted requests with a Cloudflare interstitial; it is reachable in a browser.

name: DIFC Public Register
jurisdiction_notes: Dubai International Financial Centre only. DIFC is a separate common-law jurisdiction with its own registrar and courts; Dubai mainland and other Dubai free zones such as JAFZA, DMCC and Meydan maintain their own records which are non-public or only partially public.
notes: Entity name, registration number, status, legal form and registered DIFC address, with directors and shareholders shown for some entity types. The DIFC Courts publish judgments separately and are a genuinely useful adverse-information source for Gulf commercial disputes, often naming beneficial owners that no register discloses. The older difc.ae domain now redirects to difc.com. Confirm the current public-register path from the home page.

name: Espacenet
jurisdiction_notes: European Patent Office aggregation covering over 100 patent authorities worldwide. Publication lags filing by roughly 18 months, so recent activity is structurally invisible. Applicant name normalisation across offices is imperfect, so search name variants and transliterations.
notes: Applicant and inventor names with addresses, priority chains and patent family members across jurisdictions, plus assignment history in some national registers. Inventor names are individuals and are often technical staff, which makes patents a good route to real employees of an otherwise opaque entity. A patent family also shows which markets the applicant actually intended to operate in. Aggregation is not corroboration: cite the national or EPO register entry. Google Patents indexes much of the same corpus with better full-text search. Marked unverified because the host answers scripted requests with a Cloudflare interstitial; it is reachable in a browser.

name: Estonia e-Business Register
jurisdiction_notes: Estonia. Free search of companies, board members and shareholders with annual reports available at no charge. Estonia historically published beneficial owner declarations openly; access to that specific dataset was affected by the 2022 CJEU ruling, so confirm what the register currently returns.
notes: Board members, shareholders with holdings, filed annual reports and a person-level search across appointments. Estonia's e-Residency programme has produced a large population of foreign-controlled Estonian companies, which makes this register disproportionately useful for tracing non-Estonian operators who wanted an EU footprint cheaply. Free annual reports mean you can often read actual financials without paying anyone. The site root redirects to a language-prefixed path.

name: EU e-Justice Business Registers
jurisdiction_notes: Covers EU member states and EEA participants through the Business Registers Interconnection System. Returns a thin standardised record and links to the national register; document fees, language and access rules remain national.
notes: Use it to work out which national register holds an entity and to confirm registration number and status across borders. It is a routing layer, not a data source - aggregation is not corroboration, and the substance and the citation both belong to the national register. Cross-border branch coverage is patchy and translations of legal form are approximate. The site root opens on a language-selection page before the register section.

name: Find Case Law
jurisdiction_notes: England and Wales court and tribunal judgments from 2001 onward with older Supreme Court and Privy Council material. This is a judgment archive, not a docket system - a case that settled, was withdrawn or was struck out may leave no judgment at all.
notes: Free full-text judgment search from The National Archives. Judgments name parties, directors and sums and often describe the underlying commercial conduct in forensic detail, which makes this one of the richest free adverse-information sources for UK-connected companies and their officers. Absence of a judgment is not absence of litigation - record it as a negative result, not a clean bill of health.

name: FINRA BrokerCheck
jurisdiction_notes: US securities industry only. Covers FINRA-registered brokers and broker-dealer firms; investment advisers are on the SEC adviser disclosure system instead and some individuals appear on both.
notes: Employment history, state registrations, exams passed, and disclosed customer complaints, regulatory actions, terminations and personal bankruptcies. One of the few free sources that ties a named individual to a firm, a date range and a regulator-verified disciplinary record. Full reports download as PDF and are worth archiving because disclosures can be expunged.

name: Florida Sunbiz
jurisdiction_notes: Florida. One of the most open US state registers: free search by entity name, by officer or director name, by registered agent name and by address, with free scanned filing images.
notes: Officer and director name search is the key capability - it pivots from a person to every Florida entity they are listed on, which most state registers do not allow. Annual reports list officers, addresses and the federal employer identification number. Address search finds entity clusters at a single suite number. This is usually the fastest free way to map a US operator's portfolio of entities. Marked unverified because the host answers scripted requests with a Cloudflare interstitial; it is reachable in a browser.

name: France Annuaire des Entreprises
jurisdiction_notes: France. Free state-run search over the SIREN and SIRET base and the Registre National des Entreprises. Access to beneficial ownership declarations was restricted following the 2022 CJEU ruling. Individual entrepreneurs may opt out of public listing, and small companies can file accounts confidentially so the figures are withheld even though the filing exists.
notes: SIREN and SIRET identifiers, NAF activity code, establishment addresses, legal form, officer names and links to filed accounts. Court-registry documents and Kbis extracts are sold through Infogreffe. BODACC publishes insolvency, change-of-control and disposal notices and is the French analogue of The Gazette. A SIRET identifies a specific establishment, a SIREN the legal entity - do not conflate them. Marked unverified because the host returned an unbounded redirect loop to scripted requests; it is reachable in a browser.

name: GDELT Project
jurisdiction_notes: Global news monitoring across many languages with machine translation. Coverage skews to outlets that publish online, so regions with weak digital news presence are under-represented, and machine-coded entities, themes and tone scores carry real error rates.
notes: Free large-scale adverse-media sweep: article-level search plus event and tone datasets queryable through BigQuery and a public API. Use it to establish that coverage exists and in which outlets and languages, then read the original articles. Aggregation is not corroboration: never cite a GDELT-extracted entity, event code or sentiment score as a finding - cite the article. Its main advantage over an English-language search is non-English adverse media, which is where most cross-border reputational risk actually surfaces.

name: Germany Handelsregister
jurisdiction_notes: Germany, maintained by the local courts and aggregated at the federal portal. Since August 2022 retrieval of register extracts and filed documents has been free, replacing the previous per-document fee. Managing directors are visible and the shareholder list of a GmbH is a filed public document - genuine direct ownership data, which most registers do not provide.
notes: Chronological and current extracts, articles of association, and the Gesellschafterliste shareholder list. The shareholder list is the single most valuable document here because it names direct shareholders with their holdings and is updated on every transfer. Financial statements are published separately in the Bundesanzeiger. Search matches the legal name fairly strictly - try spelling variants and search by register court plus HRB number when you have it. Marked unverified because no TLS connection to the host completed from this environment on repeated attempts; treat reachability as environment-dependent and retest before planning around it.

name: GLEIF Global LEI Index
jurisdiction_notes: Global. Coverage is limited to entities that obtained a Legal Entity Identifier, which is driven by derivatives and securities reporting obligations, so private companies with no market activity are usually absent.
notes: Authoritative mapping of legal entity to LEI, legal name, registered address and local registry identifier. Level 2 relationship data records direct and ultimate accounting parent where reported, which is the closest thing to a free cross-border group-structure source. A concatenated reference file and a public API are published from the main GLEIF site - confirm current URLs there rather than assuming.

name: Hong Kong Companies Registry
jurisdiction_notes: Hong Kong. The Cyber Search Centre offers free company name and number lookup; document images and director particulars are charged per item and generally require a registered account. Under the phased New Inspection Regime beginning in December 2023, directors' full identification numbers and usual residential addresses are withheld from public copies of filed documents, with correspondence addresses and partial identification numbers shown instead.
notes: Annual returns list directors, the company secretary and shareholders with holdings, which remains valuable even under the redacted regime. Hong Kong is the standard intermediary layer between BVI or Samoa holding companies and mainland Chinese operating companies, so the annual return frequently names the offshore parent that the offshore jurisdiction itself will not disclose. Charges are per document and accumulate - plan which filings you actually need before pulling. The recorded host redirects into the registry's current e-services application.

name: ICIJ Offshore Leaks Database
jurisdiction_notes: Covers offshore incorporation agents in the BVI, Panama, the Bahamas, Singapore and elsewhere. Data is historical and ends at the date of each leak; it does not reflect current ownership or current directors.
notes: Combined Offshore Leaks, Panama Papers, Bahamas Leaks, Paradise Papers and Pandora Papers entity graph showing officers, intermediaries and addresses with the links between them. ICIJ states explicitly that presence is not evidence of wrongdoing - treat a hit as a lead needing corroboration and always record the leak date as the as-of date of the relationship.

name: Ireland Companies Registration Office CORE
jurisdiction_notes: Republic of Ireland. Company and business-name search is free; director search and document images are charged per item and normally require a registered CORE account. Directors are public with a service address and partial date of birth.
notes: Annual returns with abridged or full accounts, director and secretary appointments and resignations, and mortgages and charges. Ireland is a very common holding-company jurisdiction, so the director list is often the fastest bridge from an Irish entity to a UK or US parent. Beneficial ownership is not held here - it sits on the separate RBO with restricted access. Marked unverified because the host answers scripted requests with a Cloudflare interstitial; it is reachable in a browser.

name: Ireland Register of Beneficial Ownership
jurisdiction_notes: Republic of Ireland. Following the Court of Justice of the EU ruling in joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 in November 2022, unrestricted public access to EU beneficial ownership registers was struck down. Ireland restricted RBO access to designated persons with anti-money-laundering obligations and to competent authorities. A general researcher will not get in; a regulated obliged entity conducting customer due diligence can apply.
notes: Holds beneficial owners above 25 percent for Irish companies and industrial and provident societies. The same ruling closed or restricted public beneficial ownership registers across most EU member states - assume EU beneficial ownership is not openly searchable unless a specific state demonstrably says otherwise. The EU anti-money-laundering package is expected to restore access for those with a legitimate interest; confirm the current national position rather than assuming either way.

name: IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search
jurisdiction_notes: US federal tax-exempt organisations. Confirms current exempt status and subsection and whether exemption was automatically revoked for failure to file. It does not cover state charitable solicitation registration, which several states require separately and enforce independently.
notes: Authoritative for exempt status and for the automatic revocation list, which is the fastest way to demonstrate that a nonprofit stopped filing. Form 990 images are available here and in bulk. Schedule B donor names are redacted in public copies, so donor identification requires other routes. Churches are not required to file a Form 990, so silence from this source is not evidence of anything. Marked unverified because the host returned an access-denied page to every scripted request tried; it is reachable in a browser.

name: Jersey Financial Services Commission Registry
jurisdiction_notes: Jersey, Channel Islands. Free basic entity search returning name, registration number, type and status; filed documents and extracts are chargeable. Beneficial ownership is filed with the JFSC and is not public, although Jersey has stated an intention to allow access to those with a legitimate interest - confirm the current position rather than assuming it has happened.
notes: More open at the free tier than BVI or Cayman, which makes Jersey the easiest Crown Dependency in which to at least confirm that an entity exists and is in good standing. Guernsey and the Isle of Man operate comparable registries with their own fee schedules. Jersey Royal Court judgments are published and are a strong adverse-information source for trust, estate and asset-tracing disputes involving structures administered from the island.

name: Netherlands KVK Handelsregister
jurisdiction_notes: Netherlands. Basic name and KVK-number search is free; extracts and annual accounts carry a per-document fee. Since 2022 KVK has shielded the visiting addresses of sole traders and small businesses where that address is also a home, so address data is thinner than older tooling assumes. The Dutch UBO register was closed to public access after the 2022 CJEU ruling.
notes: Directors and authorised signatories appear on the paid extract, not on the free search result, so budget for the extract on any entity that matters. The Netherlands is a very common conduit and holding jurisdiction, which makes the extract usually worth the fee. Foundations and cooperatives are frequently used as control vehicles here and sit in the same register.

name: New York Department of State business entity database
jurisdiction_notes: New York State. The Corporation and Business Entity Database gives name, DOS identifier, status, county, registered agent and the address for service of process. Officers and shareholders are not published and LLC members are not disclosed.
notes: Useful for confirming existence and the service-of-process address, which for small entities is frequently a genuine business or home address rather than an agent. Marked unverified because the department site resolves but the entity-search application runs on a separate host that answered a scripted request with a JavaScript bot-challenge rather than the search form - reach it from the department site in a browser. For control in New York, pivot to New York City property records, state court filings and licensing bodies. New York enacted an LLC Transparency Act creating a beneficial ownership filing requirement; the resulting database is reported to be restricted to government access rather than publicly searchable - confirm its current status and commencement date before relying on either reading.

name: OCCRP Aleph
jurisdiction_notes: Mixes public registers with leaked and hacked material. Collections carry different access levels and some are visible only to verified journalists. Handling leaked material may be lawful for journalism in the public interest and unlawful in other contexts - check it against the case authority before relying on it.
notes: Full-text search across scraped registers, court records, procurement data and document collections. Strongest on Eastern Europe, the Balkans, Central Asia and Latin America. Entity extraction is automated and noisy. Aggregation is not corroboration: read the underlying document and cite the originating register or filing, not the Aleph record. Good for finding that a document exists; poor as a citation on its own.

name: OpenCorporates
jurisdiction_notes: Aggregates over 100 company registers but depth varies enormously by jurisdiction. Officer data is present for the UK and some US states and entirely absent for others. Always confirm a fact at the primary register before relying on it.
notes: Best single starting point for cross-border company name and officer search. Data is a snapshot of the source register and can lag it by months. Free web access has been progressively restricted and bulk or API access is licensed - check current terms before planning around it. Aggregation is not corroboration: every record links back to the source register, so follow that link and cite the register, never this aggregator.

name: PACER
jurisdiction_notes: US federal courts: district, bankruptcy and appellate. State court records are not in PACER and must be pulled from each state's own system. Access requires a registered account with a payment method on file and charges per page, with fees waived below a quarterly threshold. Sealed and restricted documents are not retrievable.
notes: Complaints, exhibits, judgments and bankruptcy schedules are the densest free-text source of corporate relationships that exists - a Chapter 7 or 11 schedule of assets and liabilities names creditors, affiliates, bank relationships and insiders in a way no register does. Use the nationwide party search to find every federal case naming an entity, then pull selectively because per-page charges escalate quickly. Check CourtListener first; much of this is already archived for free.

name: Panama Registro Publico
jurisdiction_notes: Panama. The public registry has historically been free to search and returns directors, officers and the resident agent for a sociedad anonima - unusually open for an offshore jurisdiction. Directors are frequently nominees supplied by the law firm acting as resident agent, so the named individuals are usually not the controllers. Beneficial ownership is filed with a non-public superintendency register.
notes: Directors, dignatarios, resident agent, capital and incorporation date. The resident agent is the strongest available pivot - cluster every entity sharing an agent and a formation window. Panama features heavily in the ICIJ leak databases, which supply the historical intermediary relationships the registry itself does not. The www host redirects to the bare domain recorded here. Site availability and search paths have changed over time, so verify the current interface before citing a result.

name: ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer
jurisdiction_notes: US 501(c) organisations, sourced from IRS Form 990 filings and the IRS business master file. Data is only as current as the last filed return, which typically runs one to two years behind the present.
notes: Full-text search across Form 990 filings, which the IRS system itself does not offer. Part VII names officers, directors, trustees and key employees with compensation, and Schedule I lists grants made to other organisations by name and EIN - that grant graph is usually the most productive pivot for mapping a funding network. An API is offered. Aggregation is not corroboration: the filed Form 990 and the IRS record are the citable primaries, and exempt status must be confirmed against the IRS before it is stated.

name: SEC EDGAR
jurisdiction_notes: US-registered issuers, funds and advisers only. A US-listed foreign private issuer files on Forms 20-F and 6-K rather than 10-K and 10-Q, so disclosure depth differs sharply by issuer type.
notes: Primary filings: 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, DEF 14A proxies with officer and director biographies and compensation, S-1 registration statements, SC 13D and 13G ownership stakes, and Forms 3, 4 and 5 insider transactions. Full-text search covers filings from 2001 onward; older filings are retrievable by company but not by text. Use the full-text search landing recorded here rather than the older /edgar path. A JSON interface is served from the data subdomain and the SEC requires automated requests to send a descriptive User-Agent with a contact address - unidentified scrapers are blocked.

name: SEDAR+
jurisdiction_notes: Canadian securities regulators, covering reporting issuers across the provinces. Replaced the legacy SEDAR and SEDI systems in 2023 and the migration left some historical documents harder to locate than they were before.
notes: Prospectuses, annual information forms, management information circulars with director and officer biographies and compensation, material change reports and insider reporting. Canadian junior mining, exploration and cannabis issuers are heavily represented, which makes SEDAR+ a standard stop when a promoter's history is the question. Circulars often disclose related-party transactions that no register would show. Marked unverified because the host diverts scripted requests to a third-party bot-detection captcha; it is reachable in a browser.

name: TED Tenders Electronic Daily
jurisdiction_notes: EU public procurement notices above the directive thresholds, plus EEA and some third-country notices. Below-threshold contracts remain on national portals, so TED represents a floor on a supplier's public-sector activity rather than the whole picture.
notes: Contract award notices name the winning economic operator with address and national registration number, the contracting authority, the contract value and the dates. Good for proving trading activity, for building an address history, and for identifying consortium partners who do not appear in any register. Bulk downloads and an API are provided. Marked unverified because the host answers scripted requests with a web-application-firewall challenge rather than content; it is reachable in a browser.

name: The Gazette
jurisdiction_notes: UK official public record of record, published as the London, Edinburgh and Belfast Gazettes. Publication here is the legally effective notice for many corporate events.
notes: Statutory notices: insolvency and winding-up petitions, administration and liquidator appointments, striking-off notices, personal insolvency and deceased estates. Frequently carries an event weeks before it surfaces on the company record, and names the insolvency practitioner - a person who can be searched further or lawfully contacted. Free full-text search with date and notice-type filters. Marked unverified because the host answers scripted requests with a web-application-firewall challenge instead of the site; it is reachable in a browser.

name: UK Companies House
jurisdiction_notes: England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. Fully free and public including filed accounts, officer appointments, charges and the Persons with Significant Control register. Officer dates of birth are shown as month and year only and residential addresses can be suppressed on application. The separate Register of Overseas Entities discloses beneficial owners of UK property held through non-UK entities.
notes: The most investigatively useful free national company register in existence. Officer search pivots a person to every UK appointment past and present, and address search finds entity clusters. PSC entries name individuals holding over 25 percent of shares or voting rights - but PSC data is self-declared and was historically unverified, so treat it as a claim rather than a fact. Identity verification under the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act is being phased in and older filings predate it. A free-key REST API and bulk data products are published on the same service.

name: UK Contracts Finder
jurisdiction_notes: UK public sector procurement above stated thresholds. The devolved administrations also publish to their own portals such as Public Contracts Scotland and Sell2Wales, so a UK-wide sweep needs more than this one site.
notes: Tender notices and contract award notices with supplier name, contract value, dates and the awarding authority. Good for establishing that a company has real trading activity, for capturing the address it declared at the time of award, and for spotting revenue concentration on a single public buyer - which is a governance risk flag in its own right. The site root lands directly on the search form.

name: USAspending.gov
jurisdiction_notes: US federal awards only. State, local, classified and intelligence-community spending is out of scope, and some defence awards are redacted or published with a delay.
notes: Prime and sub-award recipients with Unique Entity Identifier, registered address, parent entity and full award history. Good for establishing that a shell has real revenue, for finding a company's actual operating address rather than its registered agent, and for mapping subcontractor relationships. Bulk downloads and an API are offered - confirm current endpoints on the site.

name: WIPO Global Brand Database
jurisdiction_notes: Aggregates trademark, appellation of origin and armorial data from the WIPO Madrid system and a large number of national offices including the US and EU. National coverage and update frequency vary and a national office search remains authoritative for its own territory.
notes: The applicant and representative names with addresses are the investigative payload - a trademark filing frequently names the real owner and a working address years before a corporate register reflects it, and the local law firm named as representative is itself a pivot. Image search on device marks helps connect rebranded or successor entities. Filing dates establish when a commercial intent demonstrably existed. Aggregation is not corroboration: confirm and cite the national or Madrid record, not this index. Marked unverified because the host serves scripted requests a proof-of-work challenge page instead of the application; it is reachable in a browser.

name: Wyoming Secretary of State business search
jurisdiction_notes: Wyoming. Free entity search with filing history, but the state does not require or publish member, manager or beneficial owner identity for LLCs. The registered agent is typically a commercial formation service that exists to mask the principal.
notes: Wyoming is a primary US shell-formation jurisdiction alongside Delaware, Nevada and New Mexico. Expect the search to confirm existence and disclose nothing about control. The pivot that usually works is the registered agent combined with the formation date - cluster entities formed on the same day through the same agent. Anonymous LLC marketing by Wyoming agents is itself a useful signal about the client's intent. The search runs on a separate host from the Secretary of State site, and that host answers scripted requests with a JavaScript bot challenge rather than the form - open it in a browser.

name: Arkham Intelligence
notes: Address-to-entity attribution and a transaction graph interface across several chains, with free access after registration. The entity labels are the product: exchanges, funds, protocols, government holdings and some named individuals. Attribution methodology is proprietary and not disclosed per label, so a label is an uncorroborated third-party claim - grade it C and corroborate against on-chain behaviour or an independent source before it enters findings. The platform also runs a public bounty mechanism where users request deanonymisation of specific addresses; posting or engaging there is a disclosing act and is not passive. Graded D rather than C: the labels are an aggregation of proprietary heuristics and user-submitted bounty deanonymisations with no per-label provenance, and aggregation is not corroboration.

name: BscScan
rate_limit: Web use is open; API requires a free key with tiered limits - check current terms.
notes: BNB Smart Chain explorer from the same family as Etherscan with the same interface and labelling conventions. Relevant because a large share of retail-facing token scams and rug pulls operate on BNB Chain, and because cross-chain bridge activity routinely dead-ends here if you only look at Ethereum. Sister explorers exist for other EVM chains with the same layout. Cloudflare bot protection returns an interstitial to anything that is not a real browser, so the endpoint could not be confirmed by scripted fetch and is recorded verified=no; it loads normally in a browser.

name: Chainabuse
notes: Public database of user-submitted scam and abuse reports against crypto addresses, domains and social accounts, operated by TRM Labs and consolidating what was previously Bitcoin Abuse Database. Fast way to learn that an address is already known for ransomware, sextortion, fake exchanges or pig-butchering, and reports often include the contact channel and the lure text. Reports are unverified user submissions - one report is an allegation, a pattern of independent reports is corroboration. Filing a report is a public disclosing act, not a passive lookup. Graded D because the database is an aggregation of unverified self-reported allegations, and aggregation is not corroboration - volume of reports is not evidence of the underlying claim.

name: Chainalysis
jurisdiction_notes: Access is normally restricted to regulated financial institutions, exchanges, and law enforcement or government bodies under contract.
notes: The reference commercial blockchain analytics platform used in KYC and AML work and by law enforcement, with proprietary entity attribution, exposure scoring and sanctions screening across major chains. Attribution methodology is not published and cannot be independently reproduced, which is a real limitation when a finding must survive challenge - document that a conclusion rests on a vendor label. TRM Labs and Elliptic are direct equivalents with comparable coverage and the same auditability limitation.

name: ENS
notes: Ethereum Name Service registry lookup. Forward resolution maps a .eth name to an address; reverse resolution maps an address back to a primary name, and the text records attached to a name frequently carry a Twitter or X handle, a GitHub username, an email, an avatar URL and a website - which turns a bare address into a social identity trail. Registration and transfer history is on-chain and shows who held the name and when. Unstoppable Domains and other naming systems work similarly but are separate registries with separate lookups.

name: Etherscan
rate_limit: Web use is open; API requires a free key with tiered limits - check current terms.
notes: The reference Ethereum explorer. Beyond transactions it shows token transfers, verified contract source, internal calls, and public address labels for exchanges, bridges, mixers and known scam addresses. Those labels are curated by Etherscan and are useful leads but are not independently auditable - treat a label as C-grade attribution, not as fact. Resolves and displays ENS names attached to addresses. Cloudflare bot protection returns an interstitial to anything that is not a real browser, so the endpoint could not be confirmed by scripted fetch and is recorded verified=no; it loads normally in a browser.

name: mempool.space
rate_limit: Public instance is open; heavy programmatic use is discouraged - self-host for volume.
notes: Bitcoin explorer covering addresses, transactions, inputs and outputs, fees, mempool state and RBF replacements. Good for reading a transaction graph by hand and for spotting fee-bumping and coinjoin patterns. Runs an onion service and can be self-hosted against your own node, which removes the query-disclosure problem entirely. It does not do wallet clustering or entity labelling.

name: Solscan
rate_limit: Free tier; API access is paid - limits unknown.
notes: Solana explorer with account, token, NFT and program views. Solana account models differ from EVM chains - a wallet holds separate token accounts per mint, so a single owner presents as several addresses. Do not treat those as distinct parties. High transaction volume makes manual tracing painful; filter by token and by counterparty rather than reading the raw history. Cloudflare bot protection returns an interstitial to anything that is not a real browser, so the endpoint could not be confirmed by scripted fetch and is recorded verified=no; it loads normally in a browser.

name: Tronscan
notes: TRON explorer. Disproportionately important in fraud and sanctions work because USDT on TRON carries an enormous share of low-value cross-border transfers, pig-butchering scam flows and payment-processor activity, and because fees are low enough that laundering chains run to many hops. Shows TRC-20 transfers, account resources and contract calls. Cloudflare bot protection returns an interstitial to anything that is not a real browser, so the endpoint could not be confirmed by scripted fetch and is recorded verified=no; it loads normally in a browser.

name: WalletExplorer
notes: Bitcoin wallet clustering by common-input-ownership with named clusters for early exchanges, gambling sites and darknet markets. The dataset has not been meaningfully maintained for years, so it is useful only for historical cases in the era it covers and will mislead if applied to recent activity. Named clusters are still a useful cross-check on which defunct service an address belonged to. The site responded and served its explorer front page at the time of check, but the clustering data behind it remains stale.

name: Bing Maps
notes: Worth checking specifically for the oblique aerial layer, which shows building facades and roof detail from four compass directions that no top-down source gives. Oblique coverage is limited to selected urban areas. Base satellite imagery often differs in date from Google, so the two together bracket when a structure appeared.

name: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem
rate_limit: Free access with registration; download and processing quotas apply and change - check current terms.
jurisdiction_notes: EU open data. Sentinel imagery is free to use and redistribute with attribution.
notes: Official ESA access point for Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical imagery, superseding the older Copernicus Open Access Hub. Sentinel-2 gives roughly 10m optical with a revisit of a few days, which is enough to date large events such as construction, flooding, fires, mass graves and vehicle concentrations but not to identify individuals or small vehicles. Sentinel-1 radar sees through cloud and at night, which matters for persistent overcast regions. Sinergise EO Browser is a widely used third-party viewer over the same archive.

name: GeoNames
rate_limit: Free web service tiers are credit-limited per account; limits change - check current terms.
jurisdiction_notes: Data is CC BY licensed.
notes: Gazetteer of place names with alternate spellings, transliterations, historical names and administrative hierarchy, plus population and feature class. Solves the common failure where a place is spelled three ways across sources or where twenty villages share a name - it lists all of them with coordinates so you can rank candidates by population and admin region. Also useful for resolving a place name in one script or language to its coordinates. Graded C because entries are aggregated from national gazetteers, other official feeds and user edits, and aggregation is not corroboration - confirm a coordinate that a conclusion rests on against a primary national source or against imagery.

name: Google Earth Pro
jurisdiction_notes: Imagery is licensed; publication of screenshots may require attribution or permission from the imagery provider.
notes: Desktop client is the only free tool with a historical imagery timeline going back decades in many areas. Also gives 3D terrain for skyline matching, elevation profiles, ruler for measuring building footprints and shadow lengths, and per-tile imagery capture dates. Web version lacks the historical slider. Imagery dates on the timeline are the acquisition date of the tile, not of the whole view.

name: Google Maps
notes: Base map plus business listings, user photos and reviews. Reviews and user-uploaded photos are an under-used pivot: contributor profiles list every other place they reviewed, which builds a movement pattern. Treat that as sensitive and scope-limited. Satellite layer is often older than the imagery in Google Earth Pro.

name: Google Street View
jurisdiction_notes: Faces and vehicle plates are blurred by default. Coverage in Germany and Austria was historically constrained by opt-out programmes; verify currency before treating absence of imagery as meaningful.
notes: Multiple capture dates per location are selectable in the time slider, which turns Street View into a change-detection tool for signage, vehicles and construction. Coverage is dense in North America, Western Europe, Japan and Brazil, thin to absent in much of Africa, Central Asia and conflict zones. Rural coverage may be years stale.

name: Iowa Environmental Mesonet
jurisdiction_notes: University-operated rehost of observations issued by national meteorological services; check the licence of the underlying network before republishing.
notes: Free archive of ASOS, AWOS and METAR surface observations going back decades, with a download interface that returns raw observation rows for a chosen station and date range. This is the practical way to get the actual hourly observation - wind, visibility, cloud cover, present weather, temperature - for the day and hour a photograph or video claims. Coverage includes many non-US networks but is deepest for US stations. Graded B rather than A because it redistributes another body's observations rather than issuing them; for a load-bearing weather claim cite the issuing service. A station is not the scene: an airport METAR describes the airfield, and convective rain, fog and snow showers vary over a few kilometres.

name: Mapillary
jurisdiction_notes: Owned by Meta. Contributor imagery is licensed CC BY-SA; check licence terms before republishing frames.
notes: Crowdsourced street-level imagery, so coverage is patchy but often reaches roads, tracks and pedestrian areas no commercial car ever drove. Frequently the only street-level source for smaller towns and for post-event captures. Each image carries a capture timestamp and a contributor, which itself can be a pivot. Faces and plates are automatically blurred.

name: Meteostat
rate_limit: Web interface is open; programmatic access requires a key and is quota-limited - check current terms.
jurisdiction_notes: Aggregates national weather service data under their respective licences; attribution obligations follow the upstream source.
notes: Interface to historical hourly and daily weather for a coordinate, with the nearest-station lookup done for you, which makes it the fastest first check. Graded C because it is an aggregator: records are merged and gap-filled from several upstream networks, and aggregation is not corroboration. Its observations and those on any consumer weather site frequently descend from the same METAR and synoptic reports, so agreement between two such sites is one source and not two. Use it to form a weather hypothesis, then confirm against the issuing archive before a finding rests on it.

name: NASA FIRMS
rate_limit: Map browsing is open; bulk and near-real-time API access requires a free key - limits unknown.
jurisdiction_notes: US government data; public domain.
notes: Thermal anomaly and active fire detections from MODIS and VIIRS with acquisition timestamp and confidence per detection. Used in conflict work to corroborate strikes, shelling, burning of structures and flaring, and in environmental work for illegal burning. A detection is a hot pixel, not a confirmed fire - industrial flares, gas plants and solar glint produce recurring false positives, so check whether the same pixel burns every week before drawing a conclusion.

name: NASA Worldview
jurisdiction_notes: US government data; public domain.
notes: Daily near-global true-colour and false-colour imagery from MODIS and VIIRS with a date slider, typically available within hours of acquisition. Resolution is 250m to 1km, so it answers questions about smoke plumes, flooding, dust, ice and large fires on a specific date, not about buildings or vehicles. Use it to establish that something happened on day X before spending money on high-resolution tasking.

name: National Collection of Aerial Photography
jurisdiction_notes: UK-held collection; copyright and reproduction fees apply to supplied prints and scans.
notes: One of the largest historical aerial photography archives, with worldwide coverage from military reconnaissance sorties including extensive Second World War and Cold War material over Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. Catalogue search is free; obtaining scans usually costs money and takes time. The right source when the question is what stood on a site before satellite imagery existed. The ncap.org.uk address redirects to ncap.org, which is the live catalogue.

name: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
jurisdiction_notes: US government data; most holdings are public domain.
notes: The authoritative archive for historical weather. Holds the Integrated Surface Database of global hourly surface observations, the Global Historical Climatology Network daily records, and a storm events database covering severe weather in the United States. This is what to cite when a chronolocation turns on whether it rained, snowed, froze or blew a gale at a place on a date, because it is the issuing archive rather than a reseller. Interfaces are dataset-specific and several search front ends exist - navigate from the homepage rather than assuming a query URL. Distance to the nearest reporting station is the limiting factor in sparsely instrumented regions.

name: OpenStreetMap
jurisdiction_notes: Data is ODbL licensed; derived published works carry share-alike obligations.
notes: The tag data is the value, not the rendered map. Objects carry operator, brand, phone, website, opening hours and building attributes that support geolocation from a single sign or storefront. The full edit history per object is public and shows who mapped what and when. For structured queries over tags within a bounding box use the Overpass API, reachable through the Overpass Turbo front end, rather than the main site search. Graded C rather than B because tags are contributed and are not systematically verified: an attribute is one mapper's claim at one point in time, so corroborate a load-bearing tag against imagery or a primary record before it enters findings.

name: Planet
rate_limit: Commercial quotas; no meaningful free self-serve tier.
jurisdiction_notes: Licensed imagery; redistribution and publication are governed by the licence, and newsroom use usually needs a specific agreement.
notes: PlanetScope gives near-daily revisit at roughly 3m and SkySat gives sub-metre tasking, which is the practical way to date an event to a specific day rather than a week. No self-serve access - pricing is enterprise, though there are education, research and journalism programmes that have granted access case by case. The free NICFI tropical basemap programme changed terms over time; verify current availability rather than assuming.

name: ShadeMap
rate_limit: Free tier with limited features; account unlocks more - limits unknown.
notes: Renders cast shadows over terrain and building models with a time-of-day slider, which handles the case SunCalc cannot: shadows thrown by surrounding buildings and hills rather than by the object itself. Useful for confirming whether a given window, courtyard or street would be in shade at a claimed time. Building height data comes from OpenStreetMap and other models, so accuracy degrades where buildings are unmapped or heights are estimated.

name: SunCalc
notes: Solar azimuth and elevation for a given coordinate, date and time, with shadow direction and length. The core chronolocation tool: measure a shadow-to-object ratio in a photo, and the solar elevation that produces it narrows the time of day, while the shadow bearing narrows the date range or the camera orientation. Two dates per year usually produce the same solar geometry, so a shadow alone gives an ambiguous pair - resolve with vegetation, weather or other evidence. Check whether the site applies local time or UTC before recording a result.

name: timeanddate.com
notes: Covers the chronolocation questions SunCalc does not: sunrise, sunset and the three twilight phases for a date and place; moon phase, moonrise and moonset, which help date a night scene when the moon is visible; and historical time zone and daylight saving transitions, which is how a claimed local time is converted using the rule in force on that date rather than the rule in force now. Also carries past weather for many stations. Returned 403 to a plain HTTP client at the time of check, so open it in a browser. The astronomy is computed from ephemeris models and is exact; the weather is only as good as the nearest station.

name: USGS EarthExplorer
rate_limit: Free account required for download; limits unknown.
jurisdiction_notes: US government data; most holdings are public domain.
notes: The main free archive for historical imagery. Landsat back to 1972, US aerial photography from the 1930s onward, and declassified US intelligence satellite imagery including CORONA which covers much of the world at metre-scale resolution for the 1960s and 1970s. Ordering scanned film products can involve a fee and delay. The interface is dated but there is no equivalent free source for pre-2000 non-US imagery.

name: Yandex Maps
jurisdiction_notes: Russian-operated. Queries and any uploads are processed in Russia; do not use for targets where that disclosure matters.
notes: Best street-level panorama coverage across Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, other CIS states and Turkey, where Google Street View is absent. Also carries business listings and reviews for those regions. Panorama capture dates are shown and are frequently more recent than Western sources for the same cities.

name: 192.com
jurisdiction_notes: Resells the UK OPEN (edited) electoral register plus directory data. People who opted out of the open register are simply absent, which is common — absence here is not evidence of non-residence. UK GDPR applies to onward use.
notes: The standard commercial route to UK name-and-address history, with historical electoral roll editions going back over two decades, which is what makes it useful for an address timeline. Also carries company-director, property-ownership and phone directory data. Credits-based, and results are teased before purchase. The underlying register is authoritative but what you get is a filtered resale merged with other files, so aggregation is not corroboration — cite the register edition, not the 192 record.

name: Ancestry
jurisdiction_notes: Subscription with a trial period. Same living-person sensitivity as FamilySearch. User-submitted family trees are unverified third-party assertions about living people and must never be cited as fact.
notes: Deepest commercial genealogical record set with digitised record images. Grade its two layers separately: scanned primary records are B, user-built family trees are D and routinely copy each other's errors, which manufactures false corroboration. Check for a source citation on every tree fact before using it.

name: Apollo.io
jurisdiction_notes: A substantial part of its contact graph derives from users syncing their own address books, so the data subjects never consented. High GDPR risk as a source of record. Treat output as a lead, not evidence.
notes: B2B contact database with deep coverage of corporate email patterns and direct dials. Free tier exists with an account and monthly credits. Good for enumerating a company's staff during an authorised phishing-surface assessment. Aggregation is not corroboration: agreement between brokers usually means a shared upstream file, not independent confirmation.

name: Bluesky
jurisdiction_notes: The protocol is public by design: posts, follows and handle history are fetchable without an account and without notifying the user. Public design does not by itself make bulk collection lawful under GDPR.
notes: AT Protocol data is genuinely open — profile records, post history and the follow graph are retrievable unauthenticated, and handle changes remain visible in the DID document, which makes it unusually good for tracking one identity across renames. Custom-domain handles bind an account to a domain the person controls, which is a hard link into an infrastructure pivot.

name: Clearbit
jurisdiction_notes: Enrichment on an identified individual is squarely personal-data processing and needs a lawful basis; legitimate interest rarely covers investigative use.
notes: Email and domain enrichment returning name, employer, role and social handles. STATUS: the homepage now reads Clearbit has joined HubSpot and the capability is being folded into HubSpot's own data product; the free logo and name-to-domain endpoints that many OSINT scripts depended on have been sunset. Confirm the product still exists in the form you need, and under which HubSpot SKU, before building on it. Enrichment broker, so aggregation is not corroboration.

name: email-format.com
jurisdiction_notes: Republishes third-party addresses without the subjects' involvement. Cite the underlying source, not this site, in anything published.
notes: Single-purpose: shows the observed email format for a domain plus sample addresses. Free and needs no account, so it is a fast first check before spending a Hunter credit. Coverage is thin outside large, US-centric organisations and samples are often years old. Aggregation is not corroboration — it republishes addresses harvested elsewhere and shows no per-address sourcing, so a match here does not confirm a Hunter or Apollo result.

name: EmailRep.io
jurisdiction_notes: Reports whether an address has appeared in breach data as a boolean and never serves credentials, which keeps it on the permitted side of the non-public-corpus rule.
notes: Single-call reputation summary for an address: first-seen age, disposable or free-provider flags, malicious-activity history, linked profiles, and breach-exposure booleans. Now run by Sublime Security. The homepage demonstrates a plain unauthenticated curl, so low-volume queries work without a key and a free key raises the limit. Good triage on an unknown sender in a phishing or fraud case. MODE: the response carries deliverability fields (deliverable, accept_all, valid_mx) whose provenance is undocumented, and nothing published establishes that they are served from stored data rather than derived by contacting the target's mail server at query time. CONTRACT.md section 9 says uncertain means active, so this row is active and does not run under a passive-only scope. Have I Been Pwned answers the breach-exposure question passively and at a better grade, so the cost of that call is small. Sourcing is opaque and the output is aggregated from undisclosed feeds, so aggregation is not corroboration; grade findings from it no better than C3.

name: Epieos
jurisdiction_notes: Performs third-party account-existence checks on your behalf; probes originate from Epieos rather than you, which shifts the exposure but does not remove it. Submitting a data subject's email to a hosted service is itself processing under GDPR.
notes: Best-known hosted email and phone to account mapper: Google account display name and profile photo, Gravatar, public calendar, and a battery of registration checks. Once fully anonymous, now account-gated and credit-limited. The Google-side output is the high-value part; treat the registration checks as Holehe-grade. The site advertises that it does not log queries and does not notify the target, but the underlying registration checks still touch third-party services, so the row stays active.

name: FamilySearch
jurisdiction_notes: Free account required. Access to records of LIVING people is deliberately restricted, and several national record sets are contractually limited to on-site use. Genealogical research on a living private individual needs a real mandate — this is precisely the kind of source that turns due diligence into a dossier.
notes: Largest free index of primary vital records: births, marriages, deaths, census, immigration. Indexed by volunteers, so transcription error is the main failure mode — open the record image rather than trusting the index entry. Legitimate in KYC work for establishing historical family and address links on deceased or historical subjects.

name: Find a Grave
jurisdiction_notes: Memorial pages for the recently deceased frequently name living relatives. Collecting those relatives is scope creep onto people who are not your subject.
notes: Free index of grave memorials with photographs, dates, cemetery location and linked family members — often the cheapest way to establish a family structure around a deceased subject. Entirely user-contributed and Ancestry-owned: dates are frequently mistranscribed from weathered stones and relationships are inferred, so agreement with an Ancestry tree is not independent corroboration. Use it to generate leads for record searches, never as the record.

name: GHunt
jurisdiction_notes: Requires you to supply your own authenticated Google session cookies. Using a Google account this way breaches Google's terms and may get the account locked. Never use a client's or an employer's account for it.
notes: Extracts what Google itself exposes for a Gmail address or gaia id: display name, profile photo, public Maps reviews and photos, and calendar where left public. Data quality is high because it comes from Google's own endpoints. Breaks whenever Google changes internals, so check the repo issues before trusting a null result.

name: Google Scholar
jurisdiction_notes: No notification reaches the subject. Automated querying is blocked aggressively — do not build scraping into a workflow.
notes: Author profiles give affiliation, a verified-at-domain email indicator (a domain pivot), co-authors and citation history. The co-author graph is the useful part for mapping a research group. Automated author-to-paper matching is error-prone and profiles merge distinct people sharing a name, so verify before relying on a publication list.

name: Gravatar
jurisdiction_notes: Nothing is disclosed to the target: you hash an address locally and fetch a public image. Profile fields are published deliberately by the account holder.
notes: Hash the lowercased trimmed address (historically MD5, SHA-256 now also supported) and request the avatar. A hit proves the address was registered with Gravatar and often exposes a public profile carrying a display name, linked accounts and additional verified emails. Silent and cheap, run it early on any email. Absence proves nothing. WordPress, Stack Overflow and many forums back onto it.

name: Holehe
jurisdiction_notes: Uses password-reset and registration endpoints. In several jurisdictions probing an authentication flow for an account you do not own is arguably unauthorised access (US CFAA, UK Computer Misuse Act). Get it named in scope in writing before use.
notes: Tells you which sites an email address is registered on. Noisy in the worst way: several modules trip reset or verification emails to the target's inbox, so it can tip the target off directly. Never run it under a passive-only scope. Module coverage rots as sites change flows, and many checks fail silently to false.

name: Hunter.io
jurisdiction_notes: Aggregates addresses crawled from public pages. GDPR Art.14 notification duties can attach when you obtain an EU data subject's address from a third party rather than from them.
notes: Primary use is corporate email PATTERN inference: Domain Search returns the observed format (first.last@, flast@) with a confidence score and a source URL per address, which is the part that makes it citable. Domain Search and Email Finder are index lookups and passive. The separate Email Verifier performs live MX and SMTP checks against the target's own mail server and is ACTIVE — do not call it under a passive-only scope.

name: Hunter.io Email Verifier
rate_limit: free tier is a small monthly verification allowance
jurisdiction_notes: Unsolicited SMTP traffic to a mail server you do not own. Inside an authorised engagement this is fine; outside one it is traffic to infrastructure you have no permission to touch.
notes: Split out from the Hunter.io row because the mode differs and the distinction is the one people get wrong. Domain Search and Email Finder are index lookups and passive; the Verifier performs live MX and SMTP checks against the target's own mail server, so the connection lands in that server's logs and can alert a security team. ACTIVE - never call it under a passive-only scope. Catch-all domains return inconclusive rather than negative, so a positive result on a catch-all domain says nothing about the specific mailbox. NeverBounce is the direct equivalent.

name: Keybase
jurisdiction_notes: Proofs are published voluntarily by the account holder for exactly this purpose, so reading them is uncontroversial.
notes: Cryptographically signed identity proofs binding a username to accounts on other platforms, to domains, and to a PGP key. A validating proof is one of the very few HARD cross-platform links available — a named linking datapoint in the sense the identity-confusion guard requires. Acquired by Zoom in 2020 and effectively unmaintained since; existing proofs still resolve but coverage stopped growing, so absence means nothing.

name: Legacy.com
jurisdiction_notes: Obituaries are family-published and routinely name surviving relatives, employers and towns. Treat named survivors as out of scope unless the case question actually reaches them.
notes: Aggregates obituaries from thousands of US and Canadian newspaper and funeral-home partners, with older items sitting behind the originating paper. An obituary is a dense identity document: name variants, date and place of death, employer, military service, family. Family-submitted and therefore unverified, and paid death notices can contain deliberate omissions. Cite the originating newspaper, not the aggregator page.

name: LexisNexis Accurint
jurisdiction_notes: US. Same GLBA and DPPA permissible-purpose gate and the same credentialing as CLEAR; misuse has led to enforcement against individual investigators. Searches are logged. FCRA-regulated products exist as a SEPARATE offering — the standard investigative product is not one, so do not use it for eligibility decisions.
notes: The main competitor to CLEAR and the other half of the US investigative-data duopoly.
